A [process-bigraph](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/process-bigraph) wrapper
for the **Innate Immune Response Agent-Based Model (IIRABM)** of An & Cockrell —
the real C++ simulator, not a mock or a from-scratch reimplementation. It bridges
the genuine agent-based model into a pbg `Process` so the inflammatory/sepsis
dynamics can be composed, run, and inspected through the
[vivarium-workbench](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/vivarium-workbench)
like any other Vivarium simulator, and uses it to reproduce:

> Cockrell RC, An G. *Examining the controllability of sepsis using genetic
> algorithms on an agent-based model of systemic inflammation.*
> PLoS Comput Biol 14(2): e1005876 (2018).
> <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005876>

> **Wraps the real IIRABM.** The upstream C++ (`bitbucket.org/cockrell/iirabm_public`,
> GPLv2+) is vendored under `vendor/` and compiled on first use; a small reproducible
> port (`vendor/patch_iirabm.py`) only replaces the removed MPI C++ bindings with a
> serial single-run driver. **The physics — the agent loop and cell/cytokine rules —
> is byte-for-byte upstream.** Every trajectory below is produced by the original model.

The IIRABM is a 2-D agent-based model of the endothelial–blood interface simulating
the human innate inflammatory response to injury/infection. Depending on five
parameters (injury size, microbial invasiveness, microbial toxigenesis, environmental
toxicity, host resilience) the *in silico* patient heals or dies of overwhelming
inflammation (sepsis). The paper searches — with a genetic algorithm — for multi-stage
cytokine interventions that steer the system from death back to health.

## Install

```bash
# development (editable)
uv venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest                    # fast tests (slow sims deselected by default)
pytest -m slow            # the full 20-seed mortality-regime check (~minutes)
```

Building the IIRABM binary needs a C++11 compiler (`c++` / `clang++` / `g++`); it is
compiled automatically on first use and cached under `vendor/_build/`. **No MPI
required** — replicates run as independent processes, parallelised in Python.

> Once installed, the process registers via `viva_iirabm.core.build_core()`.

## The composite generators

Each generator builds one pbg composite wrapping a real IIRABM simulation. They are
the dashboard-visible entry points (Composites tab):

| Generator | Module | What it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `iirabm_baseline` | `viva_iirabm.composites.sepsis` | One untreated IIRABM sepsis trajectory. Defaults = the paper's trained 82%-death parameter set (injury 33, invasiveness 2, toxigenesis 5, env-toxicity 2, resilience 0.1) |
| `iirabm_treated` | `viva_iirabm.composites.sepsis` | One trajectory under a named multi-stage cytokine intervention (e.g. the digitized Fig-2 GA solution) |

The real bridge lives in `viva_iirabm/runtime.py` (builds + drives the binary) and
`viva_iirabm/processes.py` (`IIRABMProcess` — runs the real sim once and replays the
trajectory per interval as deltas). `viva_iirabm/ga.py` is a reduced-scale
reproduction of the paper's genetic algorithm; `viva_iirabm/interventions.py` holds
the digitized Fig-2 intervention.

## The reproduction investigation

`workspace/investigations/iirabm/` is the four-study arc that asks: *can the key
results of Cockrell & An (2018) be reproduced from the genuine IIRABM?* Each study
maps to a paper figure, runs against the real model, and commits an interactive
figure with an honest verdict:

1. **`fig6-stochastic-trajectories`** — 100 stochastic replicates of the trained
   parameter set, classified death/heal (Fig 6). **Verdict: supported** — 77%
   mortality (paper ~82%); a high-mortality random dynamical system.
2. **`fig4-nonresponder-dynamics`** — responder-average vs non-responder dynamics
   (oxygen deficit, GCSF, neutrophils) under a fixed intervention (Fig 4). **Verdict:
   qualified** — the population splits (5 responders / 35 non-responders); the
   *digitized* intervention is not itself population-beneficial.
3. **`fig2-ga-intervention`** — the reduced-scale GA searches the real model for a
   multi-stage intervention; its convergence, the Fig-2-style bars, and the
   mortality-vs-#interventions table (Fig 2 / Table 1). **Verdict: qualified** —
   the GA converges (fitness 2340→1048) and marginally beats untreated (77.5% vs
   80%); the paper's 82%→16% needs supercomputer-scale search.
4. **`fig3-generalizability`** — base vs post-intervention mortality across a
   subsample of clinically-relevant parameter sets (Fig 3). **Verdict: qualified** —
   the fixed intervention does *not* generalize (2/18 sets improved), reinforcing the
   paper's adaptive-medicine argument.

See each study's `study.yaml` (or the published dashboard) for the exact behavior
tests, results, and caveats.

## Reproduction status

| Paper artifact | What it shows | Status here |
|---|---|---|
| **Fig 6 / baseline** | 100 stochastic trajectories, ~82% death | ✅ reproduced (77% / 100 seeds) |
| **Fig 4** | Responder vs non-responder dynamics | ✅ phenomenon reproduced |
| **Fig 2 / Table 1** | GA-identified intervention lowers mortality | ◐ GA reproduced at reduced scale + Fig 2 digitized |
| **Fig 3** | Generalizability across 8,291 parameter sets | ◐ subsampled; fixed intervention does not generalize |

The paper's GA training and full generalizability sweep used up to ~1,000,000
CPU-hours on Cray supercomputers; this repo reproduces the **method** at laptop
scale and is explicit about what is scaled down.

## Running a study

Each study has a `sims/run.py` runner that builds the real-model data, evaluates its
result, renders an interactive Plotly figure to `viz/*.html`, and records the run
into the workspace's `.pbg/runs.jsonl`:

```bash
python workspace/studies/fig6-stochastic-trajectories/sims/run.py
# ... one per study: fig4-nonresponder-dynamics, fig2-ga-intervention,
#     fig3-generalizability  — or all four:
./scripts/reproduce_all.sh
```

`.pbg/` is gitignored runtime state — re-run the studies locally to regenerate it.

## Publishing the read-only dashboard

The workspace ships the standard static-bundle publish flow:

```bash
# build the self-contained bundle locally
bash scripts/publish_dashboard.sh reports/published/workbench "/viva-iirabm/workbench"
# preview it locally (serves at the right base path; a plain file:// open 404s assets)
./scripts/preview_dashboard.sh
```

`.github/workflows/publish-dashboard.yml` republishes to the `gh-pages` branch on
every push to `main`. **Note:** the `vivarium-collective` org's GitHub Actions are
currently billing-halted, so the live dashboard was published manually to `gh-pages`;
re-run that publish by hand until org billing is restored.

## Layout

```
viva_iirabm/
├── runtime.py              # build + drive the real IIRABM binary (parse trajectories)
├── processes.py            # IIRABMProcess — real bridge (run once, replay per interval)
├── core.py                 # build_core()
├── ga.py                   # reduced-scale reproduction of the paper's genetic algorithm
├── interventions.py        # digitized Fig-2 intervention genome
├── reproduce.py            # figure data-generators + Plotly figure builders
└── composites/sepsis.py    # the 2 generators above
vendor/
├── iirabm_upstream/V1/     # pristine An & Cockrell C++ (GPLv2+)
├── patch_iirabm.py         # reproducible serial port
└── PROVENANCE.md           # upstream commit, license, what the port changes
workspace/investigations/iirabm/   # the reproduction investigation
workspace/studies/<slug>/
├── study.yaml              # question/hypothesis/behavior_tests/verdict
├── sims/run.py             # runner: run → render → log
├── viz/*.html              # rendered interactive figure
└── data/result.json        # headline metrics
```

## Notes

- **Not a mock, not a reimplementation.** The compiled binary is the genuine An &
  Cockrell IIRABM; only the MPI orchestration was replaced with a serial driver.
- **Reproducible provenance.** The upstream sources are vendored pristine and the
  port is a documented patch script — don't edit the vendored C++ directly; change
  the patch and rebuild (see `vendor/PROVENANCE.md`).
- **Scale honesty.** The GA and generalizability results are reproduced as *method*
  at laptop scale, not at the paper's supercomputer scale; the Fig-2 intervention is
  digitized from the published bar chart (no numeric genome is given), so its exact
  effect is approximate.
- **License.** MIT for the `viva_iirabm` Python package; GPLv2+ for the vendored
  IIRABM C++ and the compiled binary (a separate process invoked by the package).
  See `LICENSE` and `vendor/PROVENANCE.md`.
